title: On the Road
subtitle: Travel safe, and remember to hydrate.

items.text: The Best Band in Town
On the Road
Panners Road

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Mark my words, Mr. APPLe, all we need to do is keep straight down this road, and we'll get where we need to be!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Did we land at the wrong airport? Sure.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Did that lorry we hitched on go bust? Absolutely.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Did our motorbike go careening into the cacti? Too bloody right.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wa-hey! Nothing's gonna slow us down!
The rockin' pirate is making her way down the sun-beaten highway, each step bringing her nearer to the distant West Coast.
She turns her back to the blazing sun, noticing her shadow shorten beneath her, then watching as it shifts behind her.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Those Foundation's fools ought to have figured it out by now—this rockin' pirate can't be beat!
She laughs, stepping gingerly across the burning stones.
Under the blazing sun, it looks as if the asphalt stretches endlessly far beyond the horizon.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: "Why did she leave without a word, so gracefully?"♪

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: "Was it something I said?"♪

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: "Now all I can do is wait for yesterday."♪
She hums her favorite tune as she makes her way forward beneath the gaze of the red cliffs above her.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain ... you ... dropped ... some ... thing.
A floppy disk tumbles out of her backpack and clatters onto the scorching asphalt.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh—floppy disk, the little gadget Sonetto gave us.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Heh, just another Foundation trinket.
She picks it up, brushes off the dust, and tucks the "lost item" back into her bag.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: If things head sideways, we'll have this little toy to make our escape.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: But ... why ... don't we just use it to go straight to Los Angeles?
His voice is uncharacteristically hoarse.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Nonsense! This is a journey, Mr. APPLe.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: And any good journey is about hoisting your sails and making your own across the wide open sea.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Not that there's much sea to go around here—

No sea at all. Only badlands and mountains and beyond the mountains, wilderness, and threaded across that wilderness are the asphalt roads of industry, stitching together civilization from coast to coast.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: But keep your chin up. We're a long way still from L.A., but we're not gonna stop till we're there.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: It'd be nice to have an airship about now. That's a groovy thought.
She pulls out the disk again—a Foundation Ritual Disk hidden among her vinyl collection, disguised as an ordinary CD.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Quick cast! Shadow Schmadow! Haha!
The Ritual Disk gives no response to her botched incantation.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain, this APPLe believes ... perhaps ...
His voice is weak, losing more and more of his usual shine and elegance.
Indeed, he seems to be struggling to stay afloat in the scorching heat and almost shriveled. Trying, with as much effort as he can still muster, to keep up with his captain's boundless energy.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Before we reach the coast ...

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain ... please ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Just think of the glorious sunshine awaiting us on California Highway 1, Mr. APPLe! We'll make it to that show in record time and rock on harder than ever!
Her ambitions remain as high as ever, even after this little ticket mishap.
They had stepped out of the plane expecting to be welcomed by the big city and ocean breeze, but instead found themselves in an entirely unfamiliar and unwelcoming place.
Now, APPLe is falling further and further behind her.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain ... if I die, bury me beneath Westminster Bridge ... please ...
His sentence trails away as he lands in a soft and squishy thud.
A remnant bit of juice sizzles on the hot asphalt as Regulus swoops him up in her hands.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oi, hey, Mr. APPLe, wake up!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Mr. APPLe—!!
Did something happen to your apple?
The car pulls off the road beside her, and the window lowers.
Need a ride?
Walking across the wilderness in this heat ain't easy.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: I'm from Gold Dust, just a little up that way. The name's Riley. What's yours?
The friendly driver waves her toward the car.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: You're lucky to meet the one and only Rockin' Pirate of the Thames—Regulus!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: But this rockin' pirate could use a bit of water about now.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Here, catch!
The driver tosses a half-empty bottle to her.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Rock on! This should be enough to save Mr. APPLe!
She twists open the cap and pours the remaining water out over her first mate.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Is that how all you Brits treat your food?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: This APPLe isn't food. He's my mate.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Alrighty then. So what brings you out here? Get lost on your way to Albuquerque? Or just decided to brave the desert on foot?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Only a bloody misprinted ticket at the airport.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh, and then, the lorry we hitched a ride with broke down, and the motorcycle hit a rough patch and skidded into some cacti, and even the bleeding tractor that found us couldn't make it more than halfway. So, now we're hoofing it.
Whether a curse or just an awful run of bad luck, misfortune appears to be following Regulus at every step.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Pfft, ha-ha-ha! Well, don't go jinxing my baby here too.
It is a playful laugh, as far as Regulus could tell.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Hold on, did you say ... "we"?
The driver glances around the rocky vista. To her mind, the only people there are herself and this bespectacled pirate.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Mr. APPLe here is my first mate.
She cradles the apple up to her chest. Her poor companion still hasn't regained consciousness under the blazing sun.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Well, your friend looks like he's seen better days.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Gold Dust is just ahead. It won't take long. So, Miss, how about it?
She honks, signaling for Regulus to hop in.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: If you need a place to stay the night, trust me, that's your only option.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: But we're headed to the coast.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Our long-short holiday is supposed to be about beaches, Dr. Papper, and rock 'n' roll!

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: I don't know if I've ever heard of a "long-short holiday."

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: But if you're bound for Los Angeles, then even if everything goes smoothly, that's going to be a long drive ahead of you. And the roads out here aren't too great.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: And if you're fixing on walking along the highway, you won't get there until sometime next week.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: So, you'll need a car. Or at least a ride.
She pats the wheel of her car affectionately, as proud as a knight atop her steed.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: So, come on now. Hop in, Miss. Don't mind the clutter. I was picking up some stuff from a friend the next town over. But I've got room for you.
She clears some of the bags and bundles, carving out just enough space in the backseat.
As she approaches, Regulus is hit with a wave of odor, a disinfectant smell that causes her to hesitate for a moment. Until she, at last, opens the door.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Smells a bit like an A&E in here.
She sniffs, like a curious cub, trying to identify the strange scent wafting from the luggage in the backseat.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Uh, could be because that friend I mentioned was working in a hospital.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Alright, ready to go!

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Don't do this, buddy. We've never let a hitchhiker down before.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Could be that your buddy's not in the mood.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: How about some music to cheer it up?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Fab! How about Something by John Lennon—

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Whoa!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I almost hit—!

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Hahaha, hang on back there. This jalopy's got some miles on it, but cut the old girl some slack.
Away From Home
Towards the Stars
Chandigarh Police Station

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Look, I've actually met a lot of honest folk ... Janardhan, I know hunger hurts more than punishment ever could. Morality only matters when people have full bellies, a place to stay, and a shred of dignity.
The officer speaks gently, as if comforting a child who made a small mistake.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Some kids will break a window, a counter, or even someone's head just so their mother won't go hungry—I get it, I really do!

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Are you that kind of man?
The man cuffed to the chair across from him sniffles and tilts his head away dramatically.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: *sob* You're right, officer ...
The drama continues. He lowers his head into his hands, choking back tears.
The officer places a hand on his shoulder and offers a single probing question.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: So ... where's the money?

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: And of course, the child—we're all very concerned about her whereabouts.
The man sobs uncontrollably, mumbling incoherent words.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: What was that? Say it again.
The officer brings his ear closer.
But what reaches up to him isn't words.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: —Aaaargh!
Teeth tear into his earlobe, ripping flesh and unleashing a stream of blood.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Let go! Let go! You damn Swine God Arcanist from Mor Pankh! Someone, get in here!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Hahahahaha!
Blood runs through the gaps in his teeth. The pitiful act is gone entirely.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: You really think I don't know what you're after?
Amid agonized screams, the door to the interrogation room bursts open.

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: Monster! Let him go!!!
Another officer storms in, pulling a black iron baton from his belt and slamming it hard into the man's gut.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: *vomiting*
The sudden blow makes him gag, and he finally lets go.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: *cough*

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Hahahaha!
The wounded officer presses his hand over his blood-soaked ear, gasping breathlessly as his colleagues lead him out to attend to the wound.
He's left alone in the interrogation room.
On the table, a headline stands out. A missing person.
—"Kanjira."
Six days ago

items.speaker: Child I
items.text: Why are we being so sneaky this time? Can't we just talk during the day? Ow—
Knuckles rap the child's head, giving him a solid but playful knock.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Shh ... Quiet down, dummy! We don't want Ms. Sherjah to hear us! Wait till we're inside the caravan. Boss must have something important planned.

items.speaker: Child II
items.text: You said the same thing last time. And what happened? Turns out you had the time wrong, and I ended up getting bit in the butt by that guard dog!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: So? Didn't I swap pants with you after that? You're so whiny.
The kids shove and chase each other. But as an adult passes by, they shrink their necks and act like perfect students.
In the night, they scurry like field mice through a melon patch to reach their destination.
Secret Base
Tiny feet rustle through the outskirts of the woods until they reach a rundown caravan.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Boss? Boss? You there? Hey, hey ...

items.speaker: Child I
items.text: *sigh* She's late again ...
"Huff ... huff ... huff ... huff ..."
The quiet caravan suddenly rumbles like the puffing breath of a giant.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Who's in there?! I—I'm warning you, get down here! This is our turf!

items.speaker: Child I
items.text: What if it's that escaped killer? Let's just get out of here ... Ajar ...
"Huff ... huff ... huff ... huff ..."

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: If you don't come out, I'm letting the dog loose!
Ajar elbows his buddy.
His buddy just points at his own chin, like, "Why is it always me?"
The kid crouches down, stretches his neck out, and curls his tongue—

items.speaker: Child I
items.text: Hiss-roar! Woof! Woof woof ...!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: You hear that?!
But the "intruder" inside the caravan ignores them completely and even starts again.
Only this time—
"Huff ... huff ... huff ... huff ..."
"Huff-chuff!"

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Finally, finally got it working!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Boss, is that you in there?!
The kids rush over, eyes wide like they're gawking at an elephant.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: You fixed up that old caravan your folks left you? Whoa, where'd you learn to pull off something like that?
The giant door creaks open, and a scrawny kid crawls out looking more like a baby bird than an ace mechanic.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Cough, cough ... Ugh, I'm choking! That kid at the repair shop wasn't lying, it seems. Not a bad trade, huh?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Hey, Ajar, you made it.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: So this is why you called us here, Boss? We're finally gonna take that caravan and steal some of the grown-ups' business?
The kids cheer wildly—but their excitement is quickly doused with a cold splash of reality.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: No, you've got it wrong, Ajar.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I ... I'm going to take this caravan and leave Mor Pankh.
Convincing the others isn't too hard, but it stirs up a wave of worry.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: But ... could it really be true? If your folks are really on the other side of the country, why didn't they ever come here to look for you?
The kids lie on the grass, staring up at the sky, fireflies floating all around them, but none of them are in the mood to catch them.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: That pickpocket who jumped off train—he looked just once at my snake anklet, and said he recognized it.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: He said back at the train station he saw a woman with the same snake! And they've been looking everywhere for their missing girl!
She pulls a missing person notice from her pocket. There's no picture, just a vague description and an age range that roughly matches her own.
And a simple drawing of a snake anklet.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Maybe ... they never abandoned me after all. Maybe they just ... forgot me.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Kanjira ... maybe he was just making stuff up? And even if it's true, what if they're not looking for you anymore?
The girl takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I have to see for myself!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: But if it really is them, will you come back?
The clouds covering the moon grow heavier.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Because ...

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: This is my home!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Boss, here, take this. It's all I "earned" this morning at the station.
The boy sits up, pulls a handful of crumpled bills from his pocket, and lays them carefully on a palm-sized leaf beside her.
Then comes the second kid.

items.speaker: Child I
items.text: And this is all I made shining shoes for those rich old men today. They tipped a lot!

items.speaker: Child II
items.text: And mine too ...
One by one, the kids empty their day's earnings onto the leaf. It isn't really all that much, but the leaf still bends under the weight.
Until it can't hold anything more.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: But you guys will go hungry!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Heh, it's no big deal. Boss, you're heading out into the big wide world. You can't go without travel money, right?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I ... I will pay you back, all of you!

items.speaker: Child I
items.text: Hahaha ... You better! When you come back, we will charge tons of interest! You'll work for us for the rest of your life!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Oh yeah! You little rascals, that's your plan, huh? Hmph! Well, when I come back, don't expect even half a rupee!

items.speaker: Child II
items.text: You wouldn't dare!
The gang piles onto her, tickling mercilessly. They roll around the grass, laughing and wrestling, smoothing the field flat.
The wind picks up.
A figure stumbles into the woods, gasping for air, barely staying upright.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: *cough* They shouldn't be able to catch up now.
A rundown caravan lies ahead—the perfect hiding spot.
He scrambles into the back, slips, and collapses behind a seat.
He's like a bear wounded while escaping from a trap. His victory is pyrrhic, and he's left too weak to move.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Ugh ... damn ...
Soon, he blacks out.
